description: Checks the Serial1 (9600 8N1) command responder: no start-up output, correctly formatted replies to ID?, SUM? and HEX? with both \n and \r\n line endings, ERR for unknown commands, empty lines ignored, and that the sketch keeps answering.
assumptions: No per-student ID values are provided, so replies are checked only for the format the handout gives (9 digits, 1-2 decimal digits, upper-case hex without leading zeros), not for the exact values.
The handout says 'promptly' without a time limit, so each reply must arrive completely within a 500 ms window after the command is sent.
A reply may end with either \r\n or \n, as the handout allows.
The digit sum of a 9-digit ID is at most 81, so the SUM? reply is expected to have 1 or 2 digits.
A 9-digit ID is at most 999999999 = 0x3B9AC9FF, so the HEX? reply is expected to have 1 to 8 hex digits with no leading zero.
Start-up silence is checked by listening for 2000 ms after the boot wait before any command is sent.

not_graded.reason: The grader does not know each student's ID, so it can only check the reply format, not the actual values or whether the three replies agree with each other.
Code comments cannot be seen on the pins.

steps.requirement: The sketch prints nothing on Serial1 before it receives a command (no start-up message).
ID? ending in \n gets your 9-digit ID (leading zeros kept) on one line.
ID? ending in \r\n also gets your 9-digit ID (the \r is not part of the command).
SUM? gets the sum of your ID's digits as a decimal number on one line.
HEX? gets your ID in upper-case hex with no leading zeros on one line.
An unknown command gets the reply ERR.
Empty lines are ignored and get no reply.
The sketch keeps answering: a later ID? still gets your 9-digit ID.
